definition: Merriam-Webster's Word of the Day for November 10, 2026 is: defer &#149; \dih-FER\&nbsp; &#149; verb To defer something is to put it off or delay it, to choose to do it at a later time. // We decided to defer the offer so that we could explore other options. See the entry > Examples: “Amelie plans to defer college for a year to attempt a mostly solo thru-hike of the 2,650-mile Pacific Crest Trail.” — Justin Souza, Noozhawk (Santa Barbara, California), 24 Sept. 2026
did_you_know: ? There are two distinct words spelled defer in English, each with its own history and meaning. The defer having to do with allowing someone else to decide or choose something, or with agreeing to follow someone else’s decision, tradition, etc., (as in “deferred to his parents’ wishes”) comes from the Latin dēferre , meaning “to bring down, convey, transfer, submit.” The defer meaning “to put off or delay” comes from a different Latin verb, differre , which itself has several meanings, including two that resound in its English descendant: “to postpone” and “to delay.” Another meaning of differre is “to be unlike or distinct,” which makes apparent another of its descendants: differ , meaning “to be different.”
